question: Does serving under real concurrent load cost measurable FIDELITY? docs/46 s29 proved divergence EXISTS under load (7 of 8 frozen prompts reproduced, the 8th did not) and s31 proved the engine is bit-identical at concurrency 1. Nobody had measured the size of the gap in KLD terms. If concurrency costs real fidelity, every throughput number in this project carries a price we have never quoted.
answer: NO. Concurrency costs 1.278e-03 mean top-20 KLD, which is 1.08x the cross-boot resolution floor of 1.180e-03 - statistically indistinguishable from simply rebooting the same configuration. It is 8.4x SMALLER than the static-YaRN rope change measured on the same probe set. No throughput or topology recommendation in this project needs a fidelity caveat attached.

design.config_held_constant: 1M static YaRN, fp8 KV, MTP, APC
design.reference: DP8 QUIET - endpoint idle, all 8 GPUs at 0 % before the run
design.candidate: DP8 LOADED - a Terminal-Bench 2.1 arm running at C16 plus interactive omp traffic, i.e. real production concurrency, not a synthetic batch
design.one_variable: concurrency. Same weights, same rope, same topology, same engine, same process family.
design.method: tools/yarn_penalty_analyze.py compare() reused verbatim, so the shared-support rule, the renormalisation and the dropped-mass accounting are byte-for-byte the same as s31 rather than merely similar

reading: The result sits ON the floor, so the honest statement is an upper bound: concurrency's fidelity cost is no larger than the run-to-run variation of rebooting the server. 59 of 384 positions were bit-identical even under load, and top-1 agreement was 98.70 %. This RETIRES the concern raised in s29 - the 7-of-8 repeatability result under load is real batch-composition nondeterminism, but it is fidelity-neutral at this resolution.
honest_limits: The load was the owner's real traffic, so its composition is not reproducible from a script; a scripted constant-concurrency version would bound this more tightly.
Measured at 1M-YaRN because that was the production config at the time; the concurrency term is not expected to interact with rope, but that interaction was not tested.
384 positions over 48 prompts in four length buckets, greedy, top-20 - the same instrument as s31 and with the same resolution, so effects below ~1.2e-03 are invisible to it.
An upper bound, not a point estimate: sitting at the floor means the true value could be zero.
